name: OpenCode
deferredBecause: The hook that looks like the right surface does not work. `permission.ask` is declared in the shipped plugin types and is never fired by the shipped binary — confirmed by live probe: a plugin exporting it, returning deny, against a real permission request, was never called. Everything else on offer is either an observation point that cannot veto, or a config ruleset evaluated before any plugin sees it. An adapter built on this could not honestly claim to enforce.

allow.note: No plugin-facing verdict API that reaches the permission engine.

deny.note: Two routes work, neither is a hook verdict: a config ruleset deny (evaluated before any event is published, so static, not per-call) and throwing from tool.execute.before. Both hold under yolo.

ask.note: A plugin cannot originate an ask. There is no API to raise a prompt from event, config, or tool.execute.before.

onCrash.note: Depends where it crashes, and the case that matters fails open: a plugin that fails to load — module throws, bad export, failed npm install — is silently skipped and the agent then runs unpoliced with no visible warning.

onTimeout.note: There is no timeout and none is configurable. Plugin.trigger awaits each hook serially with no deadline, so a hung hook hangs the agent indefinitely. Verified live.

shell.note: tool.execute.before covers model-invoked tools, but POST /session/{id}/shell executes a shell command with no permission check and no event at all. Verified live against a config that denied `rm *`.

canModifyInput.note: Mutating output.args in place rewrites what executes AND what the permission engine then evaluates — which is a capability and a hazard, since it lets a plugin launder a command past the ruleset.

exposesMode.note: No hook input carries a permission mode.

upstreamLimitations: permission.ask is declared in the plugin types and never fired. Building on it would produce an adapter that appears installed and enforces nothing.
A plugin that fails to load is silently skipped, with no warning, and the agent runs unpoliced.
No hook timeout of any kind, so a slow hook hangs the agent rather than failing.
POST /session/{id}/shell runs commands with no permission check and no event.
Mutating tool args in a plugin changes what the permission engine evaluates, so plugin order decides the verdict.
leastgrantLimitations: No adapter ships. This file records a completed evaluation, not a supported integration.
Revisit if OpenCode wires permission.ask to the permission engine, which would make a faithful adapter straightforward.
